model.dependency: EXECUTE continuously depends on SUPPORT at hour 8; MUTD=N; DTTOL is the only semantic difference between dependent inputs
model.failure: accepted A05 stochastic system FRT=300000 operating hours with seed 1 and half-hour direct repair

predeclared_hypotheses: SUPPORT begins with two aircraft and EXECUTE with a third; a fourth is a ready spare. All missions and source business rows convert cleanly and launch from the scheduled hour 8.

The accepted A05 parent observed a half-hour SUPPORT-like suspension under this seed. The changed A14 model must independently show a finite SUPPORT suspension and resumed operation with a prepared replacement. Failure onset is stochastic and is not assumed to remain at the A05 timestamp.

The no-dependency control provides a same-model failure/suspension and EXECUTE outcome reference. All five runs must be compared for identical stochastic failure and SUPPORT gap timing before attributing any EXECUTE difference to DTTOL.

If the observed SUPPORT gap is 0.5 hour, DTTOL=0 and 0.49 should abort the dependent EXECUTE before its hour-11 planned end; DTTOL=0.51 should preserve it through the gap. The DTTOL=0.5 exact boundary is measured without preassigning event order.

For every accepted run, independently reconcile failure, preparation, suspension, dependency and mission events with 32 aligned half-hour system/stock bins, success factors and terminal readiness. Any changed failure schedule, absent gap, converter error or unsupported dependency result makes this five-run comparison a diagnostic.
limits: One seed and one stochastic failure onset; this cannot prove a general DTTOL law or deterministic failure timing.
No other DTTOL values, multiple precedents, cross-unit or profile dependence, GUI visual behavior or cross-engine equivalence.
